title: From Fast Fluorescence Imaging to Molecular Diffusion Law on Live Cell Membranes in a Commercial Microscope
protocol: Dilute 10 µl of 30 nm fluorescent bead solution in 90 µl of distilled water.
Sonicate the diluted solution for 20 min.
Cut a square (1 cm x 1 cm) piece of 3% agarose gel.
Deposit 10 µl of the sonicated solution on top of the gel piece.
Invert the gel piece onto the bottom glass of a 2 cm Petri dish and flatten the drop.
Turn on the acquisition setup and place the sample in the holder.
Set camera exposure to 100 msec and EMgain to 1,000.
Wait for the camera to cool down.
Set acquisition mode to Frame Transfer.
Acquire 100 frames with 100 repetitions and auto save setting.
Focus on the border of the gel using the eyepiece and transmitted light.
Move the objective to the center of the gel.
Adjust focus accurately on a brighter spot representing bead aggregates as a reference.
Start the laser alignment procedure (select ‘TIRF setup’ in LAS AF).
Acquire 100 frames from several single spots by repeating steps focusing on isolated single spots.
Import the acquired series to a data processing program and average the stack in time.
Select a single isolated bead, taking care to choose the smallest ones to avoid particle aggregates.
Fit the selected intensity distribution with a Gaussian function using the command “gaussfit”.
Inspect the obtained residuals to verify the goodness of the fit.
Turn on camera and wait for the camera to cool down.
Set camera acquisition settings (e.g., exposure to 0.5 msec, EMgain to 1,000, acquisition mode to Cropped Mode, ROI size to 32 x 128, repetitions to 10,000).
Start the acquisition of the camera background signal.
Import acquired frame series to a data processing program.
Calculate and inspect the average intensity in each pixel to verify that the camera background is approximately flat.
In Cropped Mode, remove the first and last few horizontal lines (3 to 10 depending on ROI size) from each frame because the camera background is usually biased in border lines.
Create a histogram of the values (Digital Level, DL) in acquired images stack using the 'hist' command in Matlab.
Plot the logarithm of resulting frequency using the semilogy command in Matlab.
Repeat the operation for all selected Camera EMGain and Gain settings.
Dissolve 1 mg of DOPE in 1 ml of chloroform.
Dissolve 1 mg of DOTAP in 1 ml of chloroform.
Dissolve 1 mg of PPE-ATTO488 in 1 ml of chloroform.
Mix together 0.5 ml of DOPE solution, 0.5 ml of DOTAP solution, and 25 µl of PPE-ATTO488 solution.
Dry the mixture under vacuum for 24 hours.
Add 0.5 ml of HEPES buffer (20 mM) to the dried mixture.
Vortex for 15 minutes.
Sonicate for 15 minutes at 40 °C.
Wash a p100 dish of confluent CHO-K1 cells three times with PBS.
Add 1 ml of trypsin and store in an incubator for 5 minutes.
Suspend detached cells by adding 9 ml of DMEM/F12 medium supplemented with 10% FBS.
Seed 150 µl of the cell solution in a Petri dish containing 800 µl of the same medium.
Store in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO₂ for 24 hours.
Replace the cell medium with 500 µl of serum-free medium.
After 30 minutes, add 2 µl of liposomes solution to the cells.
Wash the cells with PBS after 15 minutes.
Add new DMEM/F12 medium supplemented with FBS for imaging purposes.
Transfect cells according to the Lipofectamine protocol using TfR-GFP plasmid.
Store transfected cells in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO₂ for 24 hours before imaging.
Work in Cropped Sensor Mode.
Turn on the microscope and wait for the cameras to cool down.
Set parameters for transmitted light imaging on both cameras: 20 msec exposure time and EM Gain of 1.
Put the microscope in Bright Field mode.
Place samples in the holder and focus using the eyepiece.
Send the light to camera 1 and adjust slits to allow light only on the ROI used for cell imaging (32 x 32 pixels).
Move a cell into the selected region and send the light to camera 2.
Draw a ROI in the software controlling camera 2 as a reference.
Align the TIRF laser according to the setup procedure.
Set penetration depth to 70 nm (approximately 70°) on both cameras.
Set exposure time to 70 msec and EM Gain to 100 on both cameras.
Select a cell using camera 1.
Send the light to camera 2 and focus accurately on the cell membrane.
Set minimum exposure, EMGain to 1,000, Cropped Sensor Mode, and 105 repetitions on camera 2.
Set autosave as FITS files.
Start the acquisition to record the image series.
Release the Gain and the cropped Mode to allow temperature stabilization.
Acquire a new cell after releasing the modes.
Repeat the last two steps in order to acquire 8-10 cells.
Calculate the average intensity of each pixel by using mean on the third dimension.
See resulting image.
Inspect the average image for cell borders or out of focus vesicles.
Exclude involved regions if artifacts are present; otherwise, discard acquisition.
Subtract the average temporal intensity from each pixel to correct immobile structures.
Calculate the spatiotemporal correlation (G(ξ,χ,τ)) using CalculateSTICScorrfunc function.
Remove G(ξ,χ,0) due to shot noise in low-light regime and detector influence.
Average G(ξ,χ,τ>0) using LogBinStack function from Supporting Material.
Fit the resulting G(ξ,χ,τ) using gaussfit function of ICS-Matlab tools to recover iMSD.
Plot waist σ(τ)^2 (iMSD) as a function of time.
Increase number of acquired frames or laser power if data are too noisy.
Average more G(ξ,χ,τ) together to reduce noise.
Open the acquired files with ImageJ using BioFormat importer plugin.
Save acquired series as Tiff sequence.
Select RICS tool in SimFCS and select File>Import Multiple Images.
Insert correct acquisition parameters and close the fit window.
Select Display>Average Intensity>CH1 and verify presence of photobleaching.
Discard the series if more than 10% of photobleaching is present.
Load again the image sequence removing the first part of the series if bleaching is high.
Check ‘Use moving average’ in Tools>iMSD>Set Parameters.
Set a number of frames for the moving average corresponding to time higher than characteristic diffusion time.
Select Tools>iMSD>Calculate iMSD.
Fit and export the iMSD from the memo pad.
Fit the first few points to extrapolate the intercept (σ0²).
Compare this value with the previously measured PSF².
If σ0² >> PSF², acquire faster to ensure no hidden dynamics are present.
Calculate the apparent diffusivity (Dapp) using equation 3.
Calculate the average displacement (R) using equation 4.
Plot Dapp as a function of R to obtain a diffusion law.
